title: Bulk report - Week 43
summary:
Capesize
The Capesize market recovered steadily through the week, with improving sentiment across both basins lifting the BCI 182 5TC from $30,518 on Monday to $34,380 by Friday. The Pacific led the initial recovery, supported by renewed operator demand, increased miner participation and talk of potential weather-related delays in China. C5 rates advanced from the low $12s to the $14.15-14.25 range by midweek.

children.title: Panamax-Kamsarmax
children.summary: The week was characterised by persistent downward pressure across both basins, with the P5TC declining consistently as the week progressed. The Atlantic remained the weaker region by a significant margin, as limited cargo replenishment, subdued grain and mineral demand, and an oversupply of tonnage continued to favour charterers.

children.title: Ultramax/Supramax
children.summary: A week of rather muted activity, however the index finished the week above last week's close. Rates in the US Gulf softened as new enquiries were insufficient to satisfy a lengthening tonnage list, with rates varying during the week from $34,000 to $31,000 for a 64,000-dwt from US Gulf to the West Mediterranean with grains and longer trips to the Far East below these levels.

children.title: Handysize
children.summary: The market strengthened modestly over the week. The South Atlantic was the strongest region, supported by healthy demand and tight prompt tonnage.
